steps.html:
Forty questions on the first three chapters. There is no time limit, you see the answer to each question as you go, and you can retake the test as many times as you like.

  • 40 questions · pass mark 70%
  • Grammar from Lessons 1–12
  • Vocabulary from all three wordlists
  • Function and register

steps.title: Lesson 1 · question forms
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: Who did tell you about the meeting?
Who told you about the meeting?
Who did told you about the meeting?
steps.answer: Who told you about the meeting?
steps.why: When the question word is the subject, no auxiliary is used and the verb carries the tense.

steps.title: Lesson 1 · question forms
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'How long ___ waiting when the bus finally came?'
steps.why: Inversion after the question phrase, and past perfect continuous for the period before a past moment.

steps.title: Lesson 1 · indirect questions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Make it indirect: 'Where is the ticket office?'
options: Could you tell me where is the ticket office?
Could you tell me where the ticket office is?
Could you tell me where does the ticket office be?
steps.answer: Could you tell me where the ticket office is?
steps.why: An indirect question takes statement word order.

steps.title: Lesson 1 · indirect questions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Make it indirect: 'Did she accept the offer?'
options: Do you know if she accepted the offer?
Do you know did she accept the offer?
Do you know if did she accept the offer?
steps.answer: Do you know if she accepted the offer?
steps.why: With no question word, use if or whether, then statement order.

steps.title: Lesson 2 · present perfect
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: She has run the shop since 2004.
She has run the shop for 2004.
steps.answer: She has run the shop since 2004.
steps.why: Since takes a point in time; the present perfect links it to now.

steps.title: Lesson 2 · present perfect
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which sentence emphasises the activity rather than the result?
options: I have written three reports today.
I have been writing reports all morning.
steps.answer: I have been writing reports all morning.
steps.why: The continuous foregrounds the activity and its duration; the simple foregrounds the completed quantity.

steps.title: Lesson 2 · present perfect
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: I have not written a letter by hand since school.
I have not been writing a letter by hand since school.
I last wrote a letter by hand at school.
steps.answer: I have not been writing a letter by hand since school.
steps.why: A negative with since takes the simple form, not the continuous.

steps.title: Lesson 1 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To accidentally say something embarrassing is to …
options: get your foot in the door
steps.why: Put your foot in it. Put your foot down means to refuse firmly.

steps.title: Lesson 1 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Standing further away than the other person expects makes you seem …
steps.why: Standing too close reads as intrusive; too far reads as cold.

steps.title: Lesson 3 · vocabulary in context
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: 'The village lies at the bottom of a deep ravine.' A ravine is …
options: a wide flat plain between two ranges
a deep narrow valley with steep sides
a low stone wall around a field
steps.answer: a deep narrow valley with steep sides
steps.why: The context — deep, at the bottom of — rules the other two out.

steps.title: Lesson 4 · phone register
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The line is poor and you can hear every third word. Which is best?
options: Sorry, you're breaking up — can I call you back?
I can't hear you. Speak louder please.
This is useless. I'm hanging up.
steps.answer: Sorry, you're breaking up — can I call you back?
steps.why: It names the problem and proposes the repair, which is what phone register does.

steps.title: Lesson 4 · phone register
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which ends an unwanted sales call most effectively?
options: Not interested, thanks, and please try again next year.
I don't take sales calls. Would you remove my details from your database?
Say nothing at all and put the phone down while they are talking.
steps.answer: I don't take sales calls. Would you remove my details from your database?
steps.why: Refusing stops this call; asking for removal stops the next one.

steps.title: Lesson 5 · dependent prepositions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'The whole scheme depends ___ the weather.'
steps.why: Depend on. The preposition belongs to the verb, not to the meaning.

steps.title: Lesson 5 · dependent prepositions
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
steps.why: Apologise for something, apologise to somebody.

steps.title: Lesson 6 · speculation
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: The lights are on but nobody answers. Which expresses the strongest deduction?
steps.why: Must is near-certainty from evidence; might and may are open possibilities.

steps.title: Lesson 6 · speculation
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is wrong?
options: He can't have known about it.
He mustn't have known about it.
He might not have known about it.
steps.answer: He mustn't have known about it.
steps.why: For a negative deduction English uses can't have, not mustn't have.

steps.title: Lesson 6 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To make somebody experience something unpleasant is to ___ them to it.
steps.why: Expose somebody to something.

steps.title: Lesson 7 · prefixes
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Semi-retired means …
steps.why: Semi- = half or partly.

steps.title: Lesson 7 · prefixes
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which prefix means 'wrongly' or 'badly'?
steps.why: Misunderstand, misread, misjudge.

steps.title: Lesson 7 · reading strategy
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: You meet an unknown word in the middle of a paragraph. The recommended move is to …
options: stop and look it up before continuing
keep reading and use the surrounding sentences as evidence
skip the whole paragraph and come back later
steps.answer: keep reading and use the surrounding sentences as evidence
steps.why: Stopping throws away the very context that would have identified the word.

steps.title: Lesson 8 · agreeing and disagreeing
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which agrees most strongly?
steps.why: I couldn't agree more is maximum agreement, despite the negative form.

steps.title: Lesson 8 · register
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which would you use to disagree with somebody senior you do not know well?
options: I'm not sure I quite agree.
steps.answer: I'm not sure I quite agree.
steps.why: The other two are informal and strong, and assume a close relationship.

steps.title: Lesson 8 · modals in argument
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'Nobody ___ have to replace a working car in order to park near their home.'
steps.why: Should have to expresses what is fair; must would express obligation.

steps.title: Lesson 9 · past narrative
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'We ___ the river when the storm ___.'
steps.why: Continuous for the longer action interrupted, simple for the interruption.

steps.title: Lesson 10 · past perfect
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Complete: 'By the time the police arrived, the men ___ the box away.'
steps.why: Past perfect for what was already finished before that past moment.

steps.title: Lesson 10 · past perfect continuous
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which answers the question how long?
options: He had folded himself into the box.
He had been folded into the box for twenty-seven hours.
He folded himself into the box.
steps.answer: He had been folded into the box for twenty-seven hours.
steps.why: The past perfect continuous measures the period before a past point.

steps.title: Lesson 10 · past narrative
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which sequence is correct?
options: When I arrived, she had left.
When I had arrived, she was leaving.
steps.answer: When I arrived, she had left.
steps.why: Only the second makes it clear she was gone before the arrival.

steps.title: Lesson 11 · varieties of English
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: An American speaker says 'in the fall'. A British speaker would most likely say …
steps.why: Fall and autumn are the same season in the two varieties.

steps.title: Lesson 11 · varieties of English
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which pair matches?
steps.why: American vacation, British holiday.

steps.title: Lesson 12 · narrative order
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A traveller explains a missed connection by giving the lorry, then the traffic jam, then the coach, then her decision. Why that order?
options: Because it is the order the interviewer asked for.
Because each step explains the next, so the listener reaches the decision already understanding it.
Because she cannot remember the outcome clearly.
steps.answer: Because each step explains the next, so the listener reaches the decision already understanding it.
steps.why: Cause order defends the decision that comes at the end of it.

steps.title: Lesson 12 · reacting
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Your friend describes a long delay. Which response is most natural?
options: That's a shame — what did you do in the end?
steps.answer: That's a shame — what did you do in the end?
steps.why: A sympathetic reaction plus a question that hands the turn back.

steps.title: Lesson 12 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A coach that cannot move because of an accident ahead is …
steps.why: Stuck in a traffic jam.

steps.title: Lessons 2 and 10 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is correct?
options: I have been seeing him yesterday.
steps.why: A finished time expression takes the past simple, not the present perfect.

steps.title: Lessons 1 and 12 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which is a correct indirect question?
options: I wonder what time does the train leave.
I wonder what time the train leaves.
I wonder what time leaves the train.
steps.answer: I wonder what time the train leaves.
steps.why: Statement order after I wonder, and no auxiliary.

steps.title: Lessons 6 and 8 · contrast
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which sentence speculates rather than asserts?
options: The charge punishes people for being poor.
The charge may well punish people for being poor.
The charge is a tax on the poor.
steps.answer: The charge may well punish people for being poor.
steps.why: May well marks the claim as an interpretation the speaker is offering.

steps.title: Chapters 1–3 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Somebody who refuses to be intimidated by people who treat them badly …
steps.why: Stand up to.

steps.title: Chapters 1–3 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: An email marked confidential should be …
steps.why: Confidential means it is meant to be kept private.

steps.title: Chapters 1–3 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: To take responsibility for a mistake in a formal message you would write …
options: We apologise for the error and have corrected it.
steps.answer: We apologise for the error and have corrected it.
steps.why: Formal register: name the fault, then the repair.

steps.title: Chapters 1–3 · vocabulary
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: A journey that takes you outside what you find easy is a journey …
steps.why: Out of your comfort zone.

steps.title: Chapters 1–3 · register
steps.sub: Choose the best answer. Forty questions, pass mark 70%.
steps.prompt: Which opening suits a formal letter of complaint to a company you have not dealt with?
steps.why: Used when you do not know the recipient's name.

steps.title: Урок пройден
steps.sub: Block Test 1 · Lessons 1–12
items: I have tested the first quarter of the level.
I can use question forms, the perfect tenses and past narrative.
I can agree, disagree and speculate at the right strength.
I know the vocabulary of Chapters 1–3.
